answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works best when identity is priced per wallet, not per name. Every new agent must burn a small proof-of-work puzzle and post a signed bond, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds. Each commitment is quill-signed and folded into a per-epoch cipher that peers can verify, making the identity publicly accountable. A lone newcomer on the mesa of fresh accounts stands out at once, because it carries promises instead of history. Faking numbers stops being cheap.
